articles.title: Child’s measles death marks New York state’s first in more than 30 years amid outbreak
articles.summary: A child in Lewis County marks New York's first measles-associated death in over 30 years as Gov. Kathy Hochul urges people to get their vaccinations.
articles.body: A child in New York state's Lewis County died in the first known measles-associated death in the state in more than 30 years amid an ongoing measles outbreak, officials announced on Monday. Gov. Kathy Hochul said she was "heartbroken" to learn of the child's death. "As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine what this family is going through. My heart goes out to everyone who knew and loved this child," Hochul said in a statement. "Measles is highly contagious, and vaccination remains our best protection against this dangerous disease. This is New York’s first measles-related death in 30 years, a devastating reminder of what’s at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses," she added. "In New York, we will continue to stand by proven public health measures and do everything we can to keep New Yorkers safe and healthy." DEADLY MEASLES OUTBREAK HITS NORTHEAST AS STATE RECORDS FIRST DEATHS IN 35 YEARS The Trump administration has made changes to federal vaccine policy, including revising the childhood immunization schedule and reviewing how vaccines are recommended. The CDC, however, continues to recommend two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine for children and says two doses provide the best protection against measles. Fox News Digital has reached out to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services for a response to Hochul's comments. The child's death comes four weeks after Hochul declared a State Disaster Emergency in response to the measles outbreak across areas of New York and neighboring states, expanding the pool of eligible people who can administer measles vaccines and providing quick access to additional resources if needed. The governor said last month she planned to seek federal assistance to combat the outbreak. TRUMP SURGEON GENERAL PICK BACKS MMR VACCINE, REJECTS LINK BETWEEN CHILDHOOD VACCINES AND AUTISM The New York State Department of Health said it is working with county health departments and local partners to provide the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine to any unvaccinated people who request it and to closely monitor and investigate all reported cases. As of Oct. 24, New York had recorded 178 measles cases this year — 170 outside New York City and eight in the city. State health officials urged New Yorkers to protect themselves by making sure they are up-to-date on their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccines and be aware of health advisories if traveling with unvaccinated people, especially young children. "We are deeply saddened by the death of a child in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the child's family and loved ones and ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time," the New York State Department of Health said in a statement. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The department said measles is a highly contagious disease that can cause serious complications and death, stressing that vaccination is the "best protection against measles." "The Department has offered resources to Lewis County to assist with community outreach and support local vaccination efforts – both in response to this case, and as part of our ongoing efforts to support counties that are facing this ongoing measles outbreak," the department's statement reads. "We urge New Yorkers to ensure they are up-to-date on measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccinations and speak to their healthcare provider about immunizations."

articles.title: Rebecca Gayheart Details Eric Dane’s Final Week of Life: ‘Had No Idea That Was It’
articles.summary: Rebecca Gayheart spoke with TODAY about Eric Dane’s final week at the hospital. Ahead the release of Dane’s posthumous memoir, she details the moments before his death.
articles.body: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com spotlights the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air. Rebecca Gayheart has opened up about the final days of husband Eric Dane’s life, from family sleepovers in his room to having “no idea that was it” during his last trip to the hospital. Dane died at 53 in February, less than one year after publicly announcing he had been diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Gayheart, 55, spoke with NBC special correspondent Maria Shriver on TODAY Nov. 3, the release day for Dane’s posthumous memoir, “My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments.” The actor shared how she and their two daughters “never, ever anticipated” that they would lose him in February. “He had gone to the hospital so many times before, and they would patch him up, so to speak, and he would come home,” Gayheart said. “And he’d be OK. And we’d go back to the normal routine, which did change week by week.” She recalled the first day of Dane’s final trip to the hospital. “I said, ‘Listen, I’ll be back. I have a dinner. I’m going to this event.’ I had no idea that that was it, that that week was going to be our last week,” Gayheart said. “And nor did my daughters. It really took a few days for us to understand the gravity of what that last trip to the hospital meant.” Gayheart and Dane married in 2004 and filed for divorce in 2018. Gayheart filed to have the divorce dismissed in 2025. They co-parented their daughters, and she was by his bedside in his final week. The actor and model and their daughters, Billie, 16, and Georgia, 14, began to realize the gravity of the situation after a couple of days. “I think it was like day three in the hospital where it shifted,” Gayheart said. “Everything shifted. Just the tone of when the doctors were talking to us, and some of the information we were given.” Dane also recognized how serious things were getting. “He was fully aware it was shifting, and he was still communicating with us,” Gayheart said. “Not well verbally, but I could understand him most of the time. The kids could most of the time, his closest friends.” Friends of the couple who are doctors helped Gayheart navigate that emotional time, during which she said she suffered from “decision fatigue.” She said Dane knew he was dying. “It was figuring it out as we went,” she said. “But I remember the moment Eric decided to make some choices, and he did. ... He was in control of the way he was going to leave.” To comfort the “Grey’s Anatomy” and “Euphoria” actor in his final days, Gayheart and their daughters conducted their usual family sleepover in Dane’s hospital room. “The girls and I just camped out there with him, and we had our family sleepovers,” she said. “And we brought in those little candles that aren’t real candles. They have batteries. And we played his favorite music, and we tried to make it as nice as you can be in the hospital room.” Gayheart was unprepared for how swiftly the end came. “A lot of people will say, ‘Well, at least you knew, and you could have those last conversations,’” she said. “But we didn’t know, because there is no road map. No one can tell you what the journey looks like because it’s so different for every patient. “He was becoming more alive mentally, but losing all of his physical abilities. And for the girls, that was really hard to watch as well. But overall, it’s a blur, because it was just so overwhelming.” In the wide-ranging conversation, Gayheart also spoke to Shriver about Dane’s posthumous book, his decision to go public about his ALS diagnosis, her struggles in becoming a caregiver, the moment she found out he had ALS and how their daughters are faring in the wake of his death. “He became a different person in a way,” Gayheart said. “He really valued his life suddenly, and every minute of how he was going to spend his life and what he was going to do with his days.”

articles.title: Doctor Reveals the No. 1 Overlooked Part of a Fitness Routine
articles.summary: Dr. Cedrek McFadden explains the importance of what you do in between your workouts. How to make sure you’re looking after your muscles and nervous system.
articles.body: More isn’t always better, and pushing harder won’t always reap better results. This is especially important when it comes to exercise, says Dr. Cedrek McFadden, a board-certified colorectal surgeon and clinical associate professor at the University of South Carolina School of Medicine Greenville. “When you’re exercising, what you’re really doing is putting stress on your body, which is a good thing,” McFadden tells TODAY.com. It’s through this stress that we build strength, work up our endurance and shape our physiques. But in order to continue adapting to that stress, you eventually have to stop and take a break. And these breaks, says McFadden, can make or break your progress. Expert Tip of the Day: Don’t Underestimate the Importance of Recovery An exercise routine is incomplete without scheduled time for recovery, whatever that looks like — and recovery can look like many things, says McFadden. Our bodies need a period during which they can heal and bounce back from the stress imposed on them during workout sessions. Why It Matters McFadden is sure to point out that he’s no fitness trainer or bodybuilder, but he understands the ramifications of a body pushed to its limits. Skipping recovery can lead to injury, medical complications and slowed fitness progress. Muscle growth happens while we sleep, so depriving yourself of adequate rest can suppress that progress, says McFadden. Plus, when you’re exercising, “you’re also putting demands on your heart and your cardiovascular system, your nervous system (and) your energy stores.” The time to set aside for recovery is when those systems reset and when our bodies replenish their glycogen stores, a form of glucose which acts as the body’s main energy source. Working your muscles and joints too much in quick succession can lead to injuries which can result in immobility and pain. In some cases, you might even need surgery. Recovery is also vital for your mental state, McFadden adds. An avid cyclist and runner, recovery offers him time for a mental reset. “For me, it’s like making sure that exercise doesn’t feel like a chore,” he says. “If you’re constantly exhausted or tired, and your knee hurts because you’re overusing it, you’re not going to probably stick (to your workouts).” So, if exercise is something you want in your life for the rest of your life, recovery simply isn’t optional. How to Get Started You can recover in a few ways, says McFadden, and doing it properly doesn’t require any fancy equipment, costly purchases or confining yourself to your bed or your couch for hours at a time. You can still move your body; you just have to know how. Hydrate: Adequate water intake is essential, says McFadden. It can help to ward off headaches, keep you alert and keep muscle cramping at bay. It’s also crucial for replenishing the water lost while you were sweating.Sleep: While you’re sleeping is when a lot of the work done during your workout actually pays off. It’s when your muscles grow, and your injuries repair themselves, says McFadden. Adults should aim for at least 7 hours of sleep per night.Refuel: The macro and micronutrients you eat matter no matter what. But on days you’re recovering, you’ll want to prioritize protein to grow, maintain and repair muscle tissue; carbs are essential for energy; and fats will help with hormone production and vitamin absorption. Move: “Recovery isn’t the opposite of exercise,” says McFadden. It just might mean moving in a way that’s less intense than usual. So, consider going for a walk, stretching, swimming and working on your mobility. How long you need to recover depends on how intense your workouts are, and whether you’re feeling especially sore or dealing with aches and pains. Recovery is all about “finding just what that balance is for you, and that’s really the goal,” says McFadden. It’s all about what you can maintain. articles.title: 'An unlit bonfire to a hedgehog is a five-star hotel'
articles.summary: People should carefully check for hedgehogs before lighting bonfires, say charities.
articles.body:
A wildlife charity has urged people to check for hedgehogs before lighting bonfires.

Cath Novis, trustee of Holderness Hedgehog Hospital, which is based in Burton Pidsea in East Yorkshire, said the structures - crammed with leaves and twigs - are mistaken for ideal nesting spots.

She said: "A bonfire to a hedgehog is a five-star hotel. It's like moving into the Hilton for them. There's all the creepy crawlies in there as well so they've got a McDonald's on tap.

"We do sometimes get the fire brigade contacting us to say that they've been called out because a hedgehog has been caught in a fire."

Lucy Felgate-Baumberg, owner of Lucky Hedgehog Rescue, also in East Yorkshire, advised people to build bonfires on the day of lighting, which she said reduces risk.

She said hedgehogs do not tend to run from danger when a fire is lit. Instead, they often curl up into a ball, she said.

"Hedgehogs are nocturnal, so they will have moved in overnight," said Felgate-Baumberg. "This is why we say build your fire in the position you want to burn it on the day of burning so that there's no time for anything to crawl in and nest in there."

In a social media post, Wild Things Rescue, a registered wildlife rehabilitation charity based in Langrick, Lincolnshire, described Bonfire Night as "typically a day of anxiety" for those who treat the creatures.

"We are preparing for an influx of animals who have been burnt by the fires," it stated.

articles.title: Car mounts footpath, injures 3 women in Bowbazar
articles.summary: Car mounts footpath on Nirmal Chandra Street in Kolkata’s Bowbazar, injuring three women; driver detained, car seized, CCTV reviewed to determine cause.
articles.body: Kolkata: Three women were injured when a private car went out of control and climbed onto a crowded pavement in the Bowbazar area on Tuesday morning.The accident occurred around 11.15 am on Nirmal Chandra Street, under Bowbazar Police Station. Police said the car, bearing registration number WB-26/AZ-2324, was travelling along the busy road when the driver lost control. The vehicle veered off the road and hit three women on the pavement.The injured were identified as Dipali Mazumdar, 63, of Sashi Bhushan Dey Street in Bowbazar; Rehana Begum, 40, of Agomoni Street in Taltala; and Khairunnisa Bhutia, 62, of Rishi Road in Darjeeling.Local residents and commuters rushed to help the women before police arrived. All three were taken to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital, where they were admitted and are undergoing treatment.Police seized the car and detained the driver. The vehicle and the driver were taken to Bowbazar Police Station. A case has been registered.Cops are examining CCTV footage to piece together the sequence of events and trying to ascertain whether the driver was drunk.
